errors.english: He is worthy of praise during the very day.
errors.why: The line completes the previous side's 'the morning that delights all beings': that very [morning] is worthy of praise among the days; it is not 'he' praised 'during the day'.

note: Bilingual Sanskrit/Tibetan side; the Tibetan verses on Śuddhodana's funeral and the monks' question are rendered faithfully, with only the opening half-line misconstrued.

errors.english: If Indra's forehead has the nature of fire,
errors.why: śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', is the standard Pramāṇa example name for an anthill (from which smoke-like vapour rises), not a literal forehead.

fix.find: If Indra's forehead has the nature of fire,
fix.replace: If the anthill ("Indra's head") has the nature of fire,

errors.english: otherwise, there would never be any actual purpose at all
errors.why: The point is that otherwise smoke would not occur even occasionally (it would lack its restricted, occasional occurrence); nothing about 'purpose'.
The Tibetan says 'some (things) such as cow dung'; 'slightly moist' is not in the text.

note: The argument on the fixed causal nature of smoke and the summary verses is followed well; one example term is rendered literally.

errors.english: That merit is acknowledged in this knowledge.
errors.why: The verse closes with a request that the addressee promise/assent (khas blangs) to this, not a statement that merit is 'acknowledged in this knowledge'.

note: Close of the Seer's birth story and the opening of the next are rendered faithfully apart from a garbled final verse-line.
Faithful rendering of the Bodhisattva's verses on anger and the king's question.
The Akṣayamati quotation on right view and right thought and the argument on vāsanā are rendered accurately; the corrupt verse half-line is honestly flagged.

errors.english: its other nature one line of text follows
errors.why: The words 'one line of text follows' are a stray artefact; the Tibetan says the existent, being established in its whole self, cannot be made into another nature (continuing on the next side).

fix.find: its other nature one line of text follows
fix.replace: it cannot be made into another nature

errors.english: it is only a refutation of the arising
errors.why: Destruction here is a mere negation (prasajya-pratiṣedha), i.e. simply the non-arising of the next homogeneous moment, not a 'refutation'.

note: Kamalaśīla's two kinds of destruction and the account of contradiction are followed correctly; one stray artefact at the end.

errors.english: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
errors.why: It is Sadāprarudita who answers, addressing her as 'Girl': that son of good family (Dharmodgata) will teach me the perfection of wisdom and skill in means.

fix.find: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
fix.replace: He said to her: "Girl, that noble son will teach me

note: Sound rendering of the abbreviated Sadāprarudita quotation, but the speaker of the key reply is swapped.

errors.english: This refers to words and such that are not mere exclusions.
errors.why: 'That' glosses the word 'non-exclusion' (anapoha) and the like, i.e. the words that would negate apoha, not 'words that are not exclusions'.

errors.english: how does an understanding arise regarding the negation of the meaning of words as exclusion from things other than those non-exclusions?
errors.why: The question is how a cognition negating exclusion as word-meaning arises from words such as 'non-exclusion-of-others'; the English misparses the ablative.

note: The apoha discussion on prameya and isolated words is mostly accurate; the opening glosses on the 'non-exclusion' words are misconstrued.
Faithful rendering of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son examples and the verse on pride born of power.
Careful rendering of the Vinaya commentary on hamstringing and evading customs through the air, with correct technical vocabulary (sthūlātyaya, māṣaka).
